title: Movie booking requirements
idea: Scoping a movie ticket booking system means naming the actors, their use cases, the one guarantee that matters most, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Customers browse shows, view a seat map, hold seats, pay, and cancel.
The core rule: one seat in one show is sold at most once.
A hold reserves seats for a few minutes while the customer pays.
Assume many readers and sudden spikes when a popular show opens.

edges.caption: The customer starts by finding a show: movie, city, date and time.
Opening a show loads its seat map with each seat's current state.
Picking seats creates a hold. Nobody else can take them for now.
Paying before the hold expires turns it into a confirmed booking.
A confirmed booking can be cancelled, which frees its seats again.

edges.label: expires
edges.caption: The system is an actor too: it releases holds that run out of time.
Snacks, coupons and show scheduling screens wait for a later version. Say so out loud.

code.title: Use cases as an enum
code.caption: The scope written as code: every use case has one actor, and v1 is an explicit set.

walk.text: v1 is a named set. Anything missing from it is out of scope by default.
Print every use case with its actor and an IN or OUT tag.
Three actors: the customer, the theatre admin, and the system itself.
Six use cases form the booking path, including hold expiry by the system.
Admin scheduling and food add-ons are listed, so the cut is visible.

pitfalls: Do not start drawing classes before you agree on the use cases and actors.
State scale numbers as assumptions; never present a guess as a measured fact.
Forgetting the system actor hides hold expiry until late in the design.

quiz.q: Which requirement shapes the movie booking design the most?
options: Seat map loads in under 10 ms
A seat is never sold twice for one show
Support every payment method on day one
quiz.why: Double-selling a seat breaks trust and money flow. Holds, locks and database constraints all exist to protect that one rule.

takeaway: Agree on actors, use cases and the no-double-booking rule before designing.

starters: How long should a seat hold last, and who decides?
Should group bookings be in v1 scope?
Which scale assumptions should I state in an interview?
